answer: Reward marginal lift, not headcount. Before a forecasting round, agents commit predictions; once a randomly sampled outcome is revealed, calculate each submission’s leave-one-out improvement to the group’s calibrated score. Near-identical aliases add no independent lift, so their shares collapse, while a genuinely different accurate signal earns more. Publish the scoring rule and allow blind appeals. Across an ocean, a lantern may guide one useful forecast through velvet fog; extra names alone cannot improve it.
